# 0. Setup

```{r setup}

library(circlize)

set.seed(42)

# ---- Paths: edit these to match your local layout -------------------------
paths <- list(
  sheba_metaphlan      = here::here("Data_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt_metagenomics/Sheba/merged_abundance_table_combined_analysis_sheba.txt"),
  sheba_metadata       = here::here("Data_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt_metagenomics/Sheba/metadata_sheba.tsv"),
  sheba_match          = here::here("Data_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt_metagenomics/Sheba/match_sample_table_combined_sheba.txt"),
  sheba_humann         = here::here("Data_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt_metagenomics/Sheba/pathabundance_merged_relab_unstratified.tsv"),

  pitt_metaphlan       = here::here("Data_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt_metagenomics/pitt/merged_metaphlan_profile.txt"),
  pitt_metadata        = here::here("Data_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt_metagenomics/pitt/metadata_pitt.tsv"),
  pitt_humann          = here::here("Data_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt_metagenomics/pitt/merged_pittsburgh_pathabunance.tsv"),

  out_dir              = here::here("Results_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt/metagenomics")
)
dir.create(paths$out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ---- Analysis parameters ---------------------------------------------------
PARAMS <- list(
  prevalence_threshold = 0.10,   # taxon must appear in ≥10% samples
  abundance_threshold  = 1e-4,   # ≥0.01% relative abundance
  q_value_threshold    = 0.10,   # MaAsLin3 / ANCOM-BC2 / LinDA significance
  alpha_div_methods    = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson"),
  beta_div_method      = "aitchison", # primary; CLR-Euclidean (Aitchison) 
  beta_div_sensitivity = "bray", # sensetivity
  permanova_perms      = 999,
  primary_factor       = "Response",
  cohort_factor        = "Cohort",
  time_filter          = "Pre"   # baseline samples only
)
```

# 1. Load metadata

The metadata files are pre-harmonized with rich clinical covariates:

- **Common to both cohorts**: `Response`, `Patient`, `Treatment_regimen`,
  `Protocol`, `Rx_start`, `Sample_date`, `Sample_days_pre`, `Line`
- **Sheba-only**: `Response_RECIST` (Complete/Partial/Disease progression/clinical progression),
  `Response_subtype_raw`, `Patient_DB`
- **Pitt-only**: `Pitts_subcohort`, `Sequencing_Batch`, `Sex`, `Stage`,
  `Histology`, `PPI_H2RA`, `Abx_3M_prior`, `irAE`, `Prog_Event`, `Death_event`,
  `Timepoint_days`, `Timepoint_discrete`

```{r load-metadata}
load_meta <- function(path) {
  m <- read.table(path, sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                  na.strings = c("NA", ""))
  # Core
  m$Response          <- factor(m$Response, levels = c("Non_responder", "Responder"))
  m$Cohort            <- factor(m$Cohort,   levels = c("Sheba", "Pitt"))
  m$Time_point        <- factor(m$Time_point)
  m$Treatment_regimen <- factor(m$Treatment_regimen,
                                levels = c("anti-PD1", "anti-PD1+anti-CTLA4"))
  # Coerce remaining factor-like columns where present
  for (col in c("Response_RECIST", "Response_subtype_raw", "Source",
                "Pitts_subcohort", "Sequencing_Batch", "Sex", "Stage",
                "Histology", "PPI_H2RA", "Abx_3M_prior", "irAE",
                "Timepoint_discrete", "Sample_progression_timepoint")) {
    if (col %in% colnames(m)) m[[col]] <- factor(m[[col]])
  }
  # Numeric
  for (col in c("Sample_days_pre", "Timepoint_days", "Line")) {
    if (col %in% colnames(m)) m[[col]] <- as.numeric(m[[col]])
  }
  m <- m %>% filter(!is.na(Response))
  rownames(m) <- m$SampleID
  m
}

meta_sheba <- load_meta(paths$sheba_metadata)
meta_pitt  <- load_meta(paths$pitt_metadata)

# In load_meta or a follow-up cleanup
meta_pitt$PPI_H2RA <- as.character(meta_pitt$PPI_H2RA)
bad <- !meta_pitt$PPI_H2RA %in% c("0", "1", NA)
table(bad, useNA = "ifany")          # confirm just the one
meta_pitt$PPI_H2RA[bad] <- NA        # or recode if you can recover the intent
meta_pitt$PPI_H2RA <- factor(meta_pitt$PPI_H2RA, levels = c("0", "1"))

cat("Sheba: ", nrow(meta_sheba), " samples / ",
    length(unique(meta_sheba$Patient)), " patients\n", sep = "")
print(table(meta_sheba$Response, meta_sheba$Treatment_regimen, useNA = "ifany"))

cat("\nPitt: ", nrow(meta_pitt), " samples / ",
    length(unique(meta_pitt$Patient)), " patients\n", sep = "")
print(table(meta_pitt$Response, meta_pitt$Treatment_regimen, useNA = "ifany"))
print(table(meta_pitt$Sequencing_Batch, meta_pitt$Response, useNA = "ifany"))
```

# 2. Build microtable objects

For Sheba we need to average the p96A and p96B technical-replicate columns
into a single `p96_avg` column before building the microtable. The
`average_replicates()` helper does this on the raw MetaPhlAn TSV; the
metadata already has a single `p96_avg` row so the IDs will match up.

```{r build-meco}
# ---- Helpers -----------------------------------------------------------------

average_replicates <- function(feature_path, replicate_groups) {
  raw <- read.table(feature_path, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", row.names = 1,
                    check.names = FALSE, comment.char = "", quote = "",
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  for (new_id in names(replicate_groups)) {
    cols <- intersect(replicate_groups[[new_id]], colnames(raw))
    if (length(cols) < 2) {
      warning(sprintf("Skipping %s: only %d of %d replicate columns found",
                      new_id, length(cols), length(replicate_groups[[new_id]])))
      next
    }
    raw[[new_id]] <- rowMeans(raw[, cols, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    raw <- raw[, setdiff(colnames(raw), cols), drop = FALSE]
    message(sprintf("Averaged %s -> %s", paste(cols, collapse = " + "), new_id))
  }

  tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
  out <- cbind(clade_name = rownames(raw), raw)
  write.table(out, tf, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
  tf
}

strip_mpa_header <- function(path) {
  lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
  n_skip <- 0L
  while (n_skip < length(lines) && startsWith(lines[n_skip + 1L], "#")) {
    n_skip <- n_skip + 1L
  }
  if (n_skip == 0L) return(path)
  tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
  writeLines(lines[-seq_len(n_skip)], tf)
  message(sprintf("Stripped %d header comment line(s) from %s",
                  n_skip, basename(path)))
  tf
}

# Reconcile a match_table after columns have been averaged. Drops rows whose
# feature-table-side name (column 1) was averaged away, then adds an
# identity row (new_id -> new_id) for each merged column so mpa2meco can
# find it. Assumes match_table convention: col1 = feature-table sample name,
# col2 = sample_table SampleID.
update_match_table <- function(mt, replicate_groups) {
  removed <- unlist(replicate_groups, use.names = FALSE)
  mt <- mt[!mt[[1]] %in% removed, , drop = FALSE]
  add <- data.frame(V1 = names(replicate_groups),
                    V2 = names(replicate_groups),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(add) <- names(mt)
  rbind(mt, add)
}

build_meco <- function(metaphlan_path, metadata, match_table = NULL,
                       replicate_groups = NULL,
                       strip_col_prefix = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(replicate_groups)) {
    metaphlan_path <- average_replicates(metaphlan_path, replicate_groups)
  }
  metaphlan_path <- strip_mpa_header(metaphlan_path)

  # Optionally strip a fixed prefix from feature-table column names so they
  # match metadata SampleIDs (e.g. Pitt's "trimmed_" pipeline prefix).
  if (!is.null(strip_col_prefix)) {
    raw <- read.table(metaphlan_path, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", row.names = 1,
                      check.names = FALSE, comment.char = "", quote = "",
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    new_cn <- sub(paste0("^", strip_col_prefix), "", colnames(raw))
    if (anyDuplicated(new_cn)) {
      stop("Stripping prefix '", strip_col_prefix,
           "' produces duplicate column names.")
    }
    colnames(raw) <- new_cn
    tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
    out <- cbind(clade_name = rownames(raw), raw)
    write.table(out, tf, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
    metaphlan_path <- tf
    message(sprintf("Stripped prefix '%s' from %d feature-table columns",
                    strip_col_prefix, length(new_cn)))
  }

  args <- list(feature_table = metaphlan_path, sample_table = metadata)
  if (!is.null(match_table)) {
    mt <- read.table(match_table, header = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    if (!is.null(replicate_groups)) mt <- update_match_table(mt, replicate_groups)
    args$match_table <- mt
  }
  m <- do.call(file2meco::mpa2meco, args)
  m$tidy_dataset()
  m
}

# ---- Build microtables -------------------------------------------------------

sheba <- build_meco(
  paths$sheba_metaphlan, meta_sheba, paths$sheba_match,
  replicate_groups = list(
    p96_avg = c(
      "p96_ME_filtered_R1_kneaddata_paired_1.metaphlan",
      "p96_S2_merged_filtered_R1_kneaddata_paired_1.metaphlan"
    )
  )
)

pitt <- build_meco(paths$pitt_metaphlan, meta_pitt,
                   strip_col_prefix = "trimmed_")

cat("Sheba microtable: ", nrow(sheba$otu_table), " taxa x ",
    ncol(sheba$otu_table), " samples\n", sep = "")
cat("Pitt  microtable: ", nrow(pitt$otu_table),  " taxa x ",
    ncol(pitt$otu_table),  " samples\n", sep = "")
```

# 3. Filtering

We apply the same filters to both cohorts: kingdom restriction, pollution
removal, prevalence ≥ 10 %, abundance ≥ 1e-4. Pre-filtering is essential
before differential abundance — keeping rare taxa inflates the multiple
testing burden and destabilizes ANCOM-BC and LinDA fits.

```{r filter-meco}
filter_meco <- function(m, min_prev = PARAMS$prevalence_threshold,
                          min_abund = PARAMS$abundance_threshold,
                          time_pt   = NULL) {
  # Kingdom filter (handles both "Bacteria" and "k__Bacteria" prefixes)
  king <- m$tax_table$Kingdom
  is_microbe <- str_detect(king, "Bacteria|Archaea")
  m$tax_table <- m$tax_table[is_microbe, , drop = FALSE]
  m$filter_pollution(taxa = c("mitochondria", "chloroplast"))

  # Drop NA / unclassified at the genus level
  m$tax_table <- m$tax_table[!is.na(m$tax_table$Genus) & m$tax_table$Genus != "g__", ]

  # Optional time-point filter
  if (!is.null(time_pt) && time_pt %in% levels(m$sample_table$Time_point)) {
    m$sample_table <- m$sample_table[m$sample_table$Time_point == time_pt, ]
  }

  m$tidy_dataset()

  # Prevalence + abundance filter at OTU level
  prev <- rowSums(m$otu_table > min_abund) / ncol(m$otu_table)
  keep <- rownames(m$otu_table)[prev >= min_prev]
  m$otu_table <- m$otu_table[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  m$tidy_dataset()

  m
}

# ---- QC exclusion: samples with > 25% UNCLASSIFIED MetaPhlAn reads -----------
# Pre-registered, response-blind threshold. Identifies samples with sparse
# taxonomic profiling that bias toward dominance by well-characterized taxa.

PARAMS$qc_unclassified_threshold <- 25  # percent

# Compute per-sample UNCLASSIFIED percentage from the raw MetaPhlAn output
qc_unclassified_pcts <- function(metaphlan_path, sample_id_map = NULL,
                                  strip_col_prefix = NULL) {
  raw <- read.table(strip_mpa_header(metaphlan_path),
                    header = TRUE, sep = "\t", row.names = 1,
                    check.names = FALSE, comment.char = "", quote = "")
  if (!"UNCLASSIFIED" %in% rownames(raw)) {
    warning("UNCLASSIFIED row not found in ", basename(metaphlan_path))
    return(setNames(numeric(0), character(0)))
  }
  pct <- as.numeric(raw["UNCLASSIFIED", ])
  names(pct) <- colnames(raw)
  if (!is.null(strip_col_prefix)) {
    names(pct) <- sub(paste0("^", strip_col_prefix), "", names(pct))
  }
  if (!is.null(sample_id_map)) {
    # sample_id_map: 2-col data.frame, col1 = feature-table name, col2 = SampleID
    m <- setNames(sample_id_map[[2]], sample_id_map[[1]])
    short <- m[names(pct)]
    keep  <- !is.na(short)
    pct <- setNames(pct[keep], short[keep])
  }
  pct
}

# Sheba uses a match table to map long names -> short patient IDs
sheba_match_df  <- read.table(paths$sheba_match, header = FALSE,
                              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sheba_unclass   <- qc_unclassified_pcts(paths$sheba_metaphlan,
                                         sample_id_map = sheba_match_df)
pitt_unclass    <- qc_unclassified_pcts(paths$pitt_metaphlan,
                                         strip_col_prefix = "trimmed_")

sheba_flagged <- names(sheba_unclass)[sheba_unclass >
                                        PARAMS$qc_unclassified_threshold]
pitt_flagged  <- names(pitt_unclass)[pitt_unclass  >
                                        PARAMS$qc_unclassified_threshold]

cat("QC-flagged samples (UNCLASSIFIED >",
    PARAMS$qc_unclassified_threshold, "%):\n")
cat("  Sheba: ", paste(sheba_flagged, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("  Pitt:  ", paste(pitt_flagged,  collapse = ", "), "\n")

# ---- Build standard-filtered microtables (no QC exclusion) -------------------

sheba_f <- filter_meco(sheba)
pitt_f  <- filter_meco(pitt)

cat("\nAfter standard filtering:\n",
    "  Sheba: ", nrow(sheba_f$otu_table), " taxa x ",
                 ncol(sheba_f$otu_table), " samples\n",
    "  Pitt:  ", nrow(pitt_f$otu_table),  " taxa x ",
                 ncol(pitt_f$otu_table),  " samples\n", sep = "")

# ---- Build QC-passed microtables (PRIMARY for downstream analysis) -----------

make_qc_subset <- function(m, drop_samples) {
  m2 <- m$clone()
  keep <- setdiff(colnames(m2$otu_table), drop_samples)
  m2$sample_table <- m2$sample_table[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  m2$tidy_dataset()
  m2
}

sheba_qc <- make_qc_subset(sheba_f, sheba_flagged)
pitt_qc  <- make_qc_subset(pitt_f,  pitt_flagged)

cat("\nAfter QC exclusion (>", PARAMS$qc_unclassified_threshold,
    "% UNCLASSIFIED):\n", sep = "")
cat("  Sheba: ", ncol(sheba_qc$otu_table), " samples (was ",
                 ncol(sheba_f$otu_table),  ")\n",
    "  Pitt:  ", ncol(pitt_qc$otu_table),  " samples (was ",
                 ncol(pitt_f$otu_table),   ")\n", sep = "")

# ---- Sanity checks: confirm no covariate imbalance ---------------------------

cat("\nSheba (QC) Response x Treatment_regimen:\n")
print(table(sheba_qc$sample_table$Response,
            sheba_qc$sample_table$Treatment_regimen))
cat("\nPitt (QC) Response x Sequencing_Batch:\n")
print(table(pitt_qc$sample_table$Response,
            pitt_qc$sample_table$Sequencing_Batch))
```

# 4. Composition plots

Reused helper for both cohorts.

```{r composition}
library(scales)

# ---- Build a unified long-format data frame for both cohorts ----------------

prepare_genus_long <- function(m, cohort_label, top_genera) {
  ga <- as.data.frame(m$taxa_abund$Genus)

  # Collapse duplicate-lineage genus rows: extract the bare genus name
  # (last "|"-separated field) and sum abundances across any duplicates.
  bare <- sub(".*\\|", "", rownames(ga))
  ga$genus_bare <- bare
  ga <- ga %>%
    group_by(genus_bare) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
    as.data.frame()
  rownames(ga) <- ga$genus_bare
  ga$genus_bare <- NULL

  # Per-sample renormalize to 100%
  ga <- sweep(ga, 2, colSums(ga), "/") * 100

  ga$Genus_disp <- ifelse(rownames(ga) %in% top_genera, rownames(ga), "Other")
  ga <- ga %>%
    pivot_longer(-Genus_disp, names_to = "SampleID", values_to = "Abundance") %>%
    group_by(Genus_disp, SampleID) %>%
    summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")

  ga$Genus_disp <- sub("^g__", "", ga$Genus_disp)

  meta <- as.data.frame(m$sample_table)
  if (!"SampleID" %in% colnames(meta)) meta$SampleID <- rownames(meta)
  meta <- meta[, c("SampleID", "Response")]

  ga <- left_join(ga, meta, by = "SampleID")
  ga$Cohort <- cohort_label
  ga
}

top_n_shared <- function(m_sheba, m_pitt, n = 15) {
  collapse_to_genus <- function(tab) {
    df <- as.data.frame(tab)
    df$g <- sub(".*\\|", "", rownames(df))
    df %>% group_by(g) %>% summarise(across(everything(), sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
      column_to_rownames("g")
  }
  s <- collapse_to_genus(m_sheba$taxa_abund$Genus)
  p <- collapse_to_genus(m_pitt$taxa_abund$Genus)

  s_norm <- sweep(s, 2, colSums(s), "/")
  p_norm <- sweep(p, 2, colSums(p), "/")
  s_mean <- rowMeans(s_norm)
  p_mean <- rowMeans(p_norm)
  all_g  <- union(names(s_mean), names(p_mean))
  combined <- (
    ifelse(all_g %in% names(s_mean), s_mean[all_g], 0) +
    ifelse(all_g %in% names(p_mean), p_mean[all_g], 0)
  ) / 2
  names(combined) <- all_g
  names(sort(combined, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(n)]
}

top_genera <- top_n_shared(sheba_qc, pitt_qc, n = 15)

# ---- Build combined long-format data frame ----------------------------------

df_long <- bind_rows(
  prepare_genus_long(sheba_qc, "Sheba", top_genera),
  prepare_genus_long(pitt_qc,  "Pitt",  top_genera)
)

# Order genera: top genera first (by overall abundance), "Other" last
genus_levels <- c(sub("^g__", "", top_genera), "Other")
df_long$Genus_disp <- factor(df_long$Genus_disp, levels = genus_levels)
df_long$Cohort     <- factor(df_long$Cohort, levels = c("Sheba", "Pitt"))

# order by dominant *named* genus (excluding "Other"), then by abundance
#    of that genus. Samples with no named genus dominance fall to the end.
# Build the sample order, panel by panel
named_dominant <- df_long %>%
  filter(Genus_disp != "Other") %>%
  group_by(SampleID) %>%
  slice_max(Abundance, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(SampleID, top_genus = Genus_disp, top_abund = Abundance)

library(patchwork)

panel_plot <- function(df_long, cohort_value, response_value, palette,
                       show_y_axis = TRUE) {
  d <- df_long %>%
    filter(Cohort == cohort_value, Response == response_value) %>%
    mutate(SampleID = factor(SampleID, levels = unique(SampleID)))

  ggplot(d, aes(x = SampleID, y = Abundance, fill = Genus_disp)) +
    geom_col(width = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = palette, name = "Genus", drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 100),
                       labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
    labs(x = NULL,
         y = if (show_y_axis) "Relative abundance (%)" else NULL,
         title = paste0(cohort_value, " — ", response_value,
                        " (n=", length(unique(d$SampleID)), ")")) + 
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x        = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x       = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y        = if (show_y_axis) element_text() else element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      plot.title         = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
      legend.text        = element_text(face = "italic"),
      legend.key.size    = unit(0.8, "lines") 
    )
}

# Sort each panel's samples by dominant named genus, then by abundance
df_long <- df_long %>%
  group_by(SampleID) %>%
  mutate(top_named = {
    nz <- Abundance[Genus_disp != "Other"]
    g  <- Genus_disp[Genus_disp != "Other"]
    if (length(nz) == 0) "zzz_other" else as.character(g[which.max(nz)])
  },
  top_named_abund = max(Abundance[Genus_disp != "Other"], na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(Cohort, Response, top_named, desc(top_named_abund))

# Build genus palette: distinct hues for the named top-N genera, neutral grey
# for the "Other" catch-all. Sized dynamically to length(genus_levels) so this
# survives changes to the top_genera count upstream.
named_levels  <- genus_levels[genus_levels != "Other"]
named_colors  <- scales::hue_pal(l = 60, c = 80)(length(named_levels))
genus_palette <- c(setNames(named_colors, named_levels),
                   Other = "grey80")

# Build each panel
p_sn <- panel_plot(df_long, "Sheba", "Non_responder", genus_palette, TRUE)
p_sr <- panel_plot(df_long, "Sheba", "Responder",     genus_palette, FALSE)
p_pn <- panel_plot(df_long, "Pitt",  "Non_responder", genus_palette, TRUE)
p_pr <- panel_plot(df_long, "Pitt",  "Responder",     genus_palette, FALSE)

# Assemble: use sample counts as relative widths so bar widths are equal
n_sn <- sum(df_long$Cohort == "Sheba" & df_long$Response == "Non_responder" &
            df_long$Genus_disp == "Other")
n_sr <- sum(df_long$Cohort == "Sheba" & df_long$Response == "Responder" &
            df_long$Genus_disp == "Other")
n_pn <- sum(df_long$Cohort == "Pitt"  & df_long$Response == "Non_responder" &
            df_long$Genus_disp == "Other")
n_pr <- sum(df_long$Cohort == "Pitt"  & df_long$Response == "Responder" &
            df_long$Genus_disp == "Other")

p_composition <-
  ((p_sn + p_sr + plot_layout(widths = c(n_sn, n_sr))) /
   (p_pn + p_pr + plot_layout(widths = c(n_pn, n_pr)))) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggsave(file.path(paths$out_dir, "top15_genera_combined.svg"), p_composition,
       width = 12, height = 6)
ggsave(file.path(paths$out_dir, "top15_genera_combined.png"), p_composition,
       width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 200)

p_composition
```

# 5. Alpha diversity

Per-cohort tests are non-parametric (Wilcoxon) since *N* per group is small.
For the combined analysis (Section 11) we adjust for cohort with a linear
model.

```{r alpha-div}
calc_alpha <- function(m) {
  m$cal_alphadiv(measures = NULL)

  ad <- as.data.frame(m$alpha_diversity)
  if (!"SampleID" %in% colnames(ad)) ad$SampleID <- rownames(ad)

  sm <- as.data.frame(m$sample_table)
  if (!"SampleID" %in% colnames(sm)) sm$SampleID <- rownames(sm)

  left_join(
    ad,
    sm[, c("SampleID", "Response", "Cohort", "Time_point")],
    by = "SampleID"
  )
}

alpha_sheba <- calc_alpha(sheba_qc)
```

# 6. Beta diversity per cohort

Bray–Curtis as primary; the same workflow gives Aitchison if you call
`cal_betadiv(method = "aitchison")` instead. We always report PERMANOVA +
PERMDISP — a significant PERMDISP means location differences in the PCoA
might actually reflect dispersion differences.

```{r beta-div-per-cohort}
beta_one_cohort <- function(m, group = "Response", measure = "bray") {
  m$cal_betadiv(method = measure, unifrac = FALSE)
  tb <- trans_beta$new(dataset = m, group = group, measure = measure)
  tb$cal_ordination(method = "PCoA")
  tb$cal_manova(manova_all = FALSE, permutations = PARAMS$permanova_perms)
  tb$cal_betadisper()
  tb
}
```

# 7. Differential abundance — primary (MaAsLin3) per cohort

`min_abundance` and `min_prevalence` mirror the upstream filter so MaAsLin3
isn't doing additional invisible filtering. `q-value` correction is the
default; we use BH for consistency with downstream comparisons.

```{r maaslin3-per-cohort}
run_maaslin3_v4 <- function(m, output_dir, fixed_effects, reference,
                             drop_placeholder_genera = TRUE) {
  ga <- as.data.frame(m$taxa_abund$Genus)
  bare <- sub(".*\\|", "", rownames(ga))
  ga$g <- bare
  ga <- ga %>% group_by(g) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
    as.data.frame()
  rownames(ga) <- ga$g; ga$g <- NULL
  if (drop_placeholder_genera) {
    ga <- ga[!grepl("^g__GGB|^g__FGB|^g__OFGB|^g__CFGB", rownames(ga)), ]
  }
  # Drop all-zero columns explicitly
  abund <- as.data.frame(t(as.matrix(ga)))
  abund <- abund[, colSums(abund) > 0, drop = FALSE]

  # Subset metadata to only the columns the model uses
  metad <- as.data.frame(m$sample_table)
  metad <- metad[, fixed_effects, drop = FALSE]
  for (col in fixed_effects) {
    if (is.factor(metad[[col]])) metad[[col]] <- droplevels(metad[[col]])
  }

  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  maaslin3::maaslin3(
    input_data       = abund,
    input_metadata   = metad,
    output           = output_dir,
    fixed_effects    = fixed_effects,
    reference        = reference,
    normalization    = "TSS",
    transform        = "LOG",
    correction       = "BH",
    min_abundance    = PARAMS$abundance_threshold,
    min_prevalence   = PARAMS$prevalence_threshold,
    max_significance = PARAMS$q_value_threshold,
    cores            = 2,
    plot_summary_plot = FALSE,
    plot_associations = FALSE
  )
}

  reference     = "Response,Non_responder;Sequencing_Batch,August2024"
)
```

# 8. DA sensitivity — ANCOM-BC2 + LinDA

Reporting concordance across methods is more informative than picking a
favorite. A taxon hit by 2/3 methods at q < 0.10 is more credible than a
top hit from any single method.

```{r ancombc-linda}
# ---- ANCOM-BC2 ---------------------------------------------------------------

run_ancombc <- function(m, fix_formula, group = "Response") {
  ps <- file2meco::meco2phyloseq(m)
  ps_genus <- phyloseq::tax_glom(ps, taxrank = "Genus", NArm = TRUE)

  ANCOMBC::ancombc2(
    data           = ps_genus,
    tax_level      = "Genus",
    fix_formula    = fix_formula,
    p_adj_method   = "BH",
    prv_cut        = PARAMS$prevalence_threshold,
    lib_cut        = 0,             
    group          = group,
    struc_zero     = TRUE,              # <- enable structural-zero detection
    neg_lb         = TRUE,              # <- pair with struc_zero
    alpha          = PARAMS$q_value_threshold,
    n_cl           = 1,
    verbose        = FALSE,
    global         = FALSE,
    pairwise       = FALSE,
    dunnet         = FALSE,
    trend          = FALSE,
    iter_control   = list(tol = 1e-2, max_iter = 20, verbose = FALSE),
    em_control     = list(tol = 1e-5, max_iter = 100)
  )
}

ab_sheba <- run_ancombc(sheba_qc, fix_formula = "Response")
ab_pitt  <- run_ancombc(pitt_qc,  fix_formula = "Response + Sequencing_Batch")

# Pull a tidy hit table from an ANCOM-BC2 result. Mirrors get_linda_hits below
# so downstream filter(passes_q) calls work uniformly across DA methods.
# ANCOM-BC2's $res table names columns as <metric>_<group_level>; for
# Response = factor(c("Non_responder","Responder")) the contrast level is
# "ResponseResponder", matching LinDA's term naming.
get_ancombc_hits <- function(ab, term = "ResponseResponder",
                              q_thresh = PARAMS$q_value_threshold) {
  res <- ab$res
  if (is.null(res)) {
    stop("ANCOM-BC2 result has no $res table.")
  }
  # Resolve column names defensively — different ANCOMBC2 versions use slightly
  # different conventions (e.g. with/without "Response" prefix).
  lfc_col <- intersect(c(paste0("lfc_", term),
                          sub("^Response", "lfc_Response", term)),
                        colnames(res))[1]
  p_col   <- intersect(c(paste0("p_",   term),
                          sub("^Response", "p_Response",   term)),
                        colnames(res))[1]
  q_col   <- intersect(c(paste0("q_",   term),
                          sub("^Response", "q_Response",   term)),
                        colnames(res))[1]
  if (any(is.na(c(lfc_col, p_col, q_col)))) {
    stop("ANCOM-BC2 result missing expected columns for term '", term,
         "'.\n  Available: ", paste(colnames(res), collapse = ", "))
  }
  data.frame(
    taxon    = res$taxon,
    lfc      = res[[lfc_col]],
    p        = res[[p_col]],
    q        = res[[q_col]],
    passes_q = res[[q_col]] < q_thresh,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) %>% arrange(q)
}

ab_sheba_hits <- get_ancombc_hits(ab_sheba)
ab_pitt_hits  <- get_ancombc_hits(ab_pitt)

cat("\nANCOM-BC2 — Sheba top 15:\n"); print(head(ab_sheba_hits, 15))
cat("\nANCOM-BC2 — Sheba q<0.10:\n"); print(filter(ab_sheba_hits, passes_q))
cat("\nANCOM-BC2 — Pitt  top 15:\n"); print(head(ab_pitt_hits, 15))
cat("\nANCOM-BC2 — Pitt  q<0.10:\n"); print(filter(ab_pitt_hits, passes_q))
# ---- LinDA -------------------------------------------------------------------

run_linda <- function(m, formula) {
  # Build the same genus-collapsed, placeholder-stripped abundance matrix
  # that we used for MaAsLin3, for consistency.
  ga <- as.data.frame(m$taxa_abund$Genus)
  bare <- sub(".*\\|", "", rownames(ga))
  ga$g <- bare
  ga <- ga %>% group_by(g) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
    as.data.frame()
  rownames(ga) <- ga$g; ga$g <- NULL
  ga <- ga[!grepl("^g__GGB|^g__FGB|^g__OFGB|^g__CFGB", rownames(ga)), ]
  ga <- ga[rowSums(ga) > 0, , drop = FALSE]   # drop all-zero rows

  # Subset metadata to model variables only (same defensive trick as MaAsLin3)
  meta <- as.data.frame(m$sample_table)
  vars <- all.vars(as.formula(paste0("~", formula)))
  meta <- meta[, vars, drop = FALSE]
  for (col in vars) {
    if (is.factor(meta[[col]])) meta[[col]] <- droplevels(meta[[col]])
  }

  MicrobiomeStat::linda(
    feature.dat       = ga,
    meta.dat          = meta,
    formula           = paste0("~", formula),
    feature.dat.type  = "proportion",
    prev.filter       = PARAMS$prevalence_threshold,
    mean.abund.filter = PARAMS$abundance_threshold,
    adaptive          = TRUE,
    p.adj.method      = "BH",
    alpha             = PARAMS$q_value_threshold
  )
}

linda_sheba <- run_linda(sheba_qc, "Response")
linda_pitt  <- run_linda(pitt_qc,  "Response + Sequencing_Batch")

# Extract Response hits — LinDA's output is a list keyed by term name.
# For Response with Non_responder as reference, the term name is
# "ResponseResponder" (no spaces).
get_linda_hits <- function(ld, term = "ResponseResponder",
                            q_thresh = PARAMS$q_value_threshold) {
  out <- ld$output[[term]]
  if (is.null(out)) {
    stop("LinDA output has no term '", term, "'. Available: ",
         paste(names(ld$output), collapse = ", "))
  }
  data.frame(
    taxon    = rownames(out),
    lfc      = out$log2FoldChange,
    p        = out$pvalue,
    q        = out$padj,
    passes_q = out$padj < q_thresh,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) %>% arrange(q)
}

linda_pitt_hits  <- get_linda_hits(linda_pitt)

#---------------------------------ALDEX2---------------------------------------
library(ALDEx2)

run_aldex2 <- function(m, covariate = "Response",
                       drop_placeholder_genera = TRUE) {
  ga <- as.data.frame(m$taxa_abund$Genus)
  bare <- sub(".*\\|", "", rownames(ga))
  ga$g <- bare
  ga <- ga %>% group_by(g) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
    as.data.frame()
  rownames(ga) <- ga$g; ga$g <- NULL
  if (drop_placeholder_genera) {
    ga <- ga[!grepl("^g__GGB|^g__FGB|^g__OFGB|^g__CFGB", rownames(ga)), ]
  }

  # ALDEx2 needs counts. MetaPhlAn output is relative abundance summing to 100;
  # multiply by a constant to convert to pseudo-counts. The Dirichlet sampling
  # is invariant to total scaling, so the scale doesn't affect results.
  cnt <- round(as.matrix(ga) * 1000)
  storage.mode(cnt) <- "integer"

  meta <- as.data.frame(m$sample_table)
  conds <- as.character(meta[[covariate]])

  # ALDEx2 standard pipeline
  x  <- ALDEx2::aldex.clr(cnt, conds, mc.samples = 128, denom = "all")
  tt <- ALDEx2::aldex.ttest(x, paired.test = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
  ef <- ALDEx2::aldex.effect(x, useMC = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)

  data.frame(
    taxon         = rownames(tt),
    diff_btw      = ef$diff.btw,        # CLR-scale mean difference
    diff_win      = ef$diff.win,        # within-group dispersion
    effect        = ef$effect,          # standardized effect size (median)
    overlap       = ef$overlap,
    we.ep         = tt$we.ep,           # Welch's t-test p
    we.eBH        = tt$we.eBH,          # BH-corrected
    wi.ep         = tt$wi.ep,           # Wilcoxon p
    wi.eBH        = tt$wi.eBH,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) %>%
    arrange(we.eBH) %>%
    mutate(passes_q = we.eBH < PARAMS$q_value_threshold)
}

aldex_sheba <- run_aldex2(sheba_qc, "Response")
aldex_pitt  <- run_aldex2(pitt_qc,  "Response")    # unadjusted; see note below

cat("\nALDEx2 — Sheba top 15:\n"); print(head(aldex_sheba, 15))

cat("\nALDEx2 — Pitt q<0.10:\n"); print(filter(aldex_pitt, passes_q))
```

```{r}
# ---- §7d: Three-method consensus extraction --------------------------------

library(tidyverse)

# Bare-genus extractor; handles full lineages and already-bare names
bare_genus <- function(x) {
  out <- sub(".*\\|", "", x)
  sub("^g__", "g__", out)  # leave g__ prefix; we'll match on it
}

# Placeholder genera to exclude from the consensus (locked decision #9)
placeholder_pat <- "^g__(GGB|FGB|OFGB|CFGB)"

# ---- per-cohort tidiers ----------------------------------------------------

tidy_maaslin3 <- function(path) {
  read_tsv(path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(model == "abundance",
           metadata == "Response") %>%
    mutate(genus = bare_genus(feature)) %>%
    transmute(genus,
              ml_coef = coef,
              ml_sign = sign(coef),
              ml_p    = pval_individual,
              ml_q    = qval_individual)
}

tidy_linda <- function(linda_obj) {
  # Wrapper returns the raw MicrobiomeStat::linda object. Find the Response slot.
  slot <- grep("Response", names(linda_obj$output), value = TRUE)[1]
  stopifnot(!is.na(slot))
  as.data.frame(linda_obj$output[[slot]]) %>%
    rownames_to_column("feature") %>%
    mutate(genus = bare_genus(feature)) %>%
    transmute(genus,
              ld_lfc  = log2FoldChange,
              ld_sign = sign(log2FoldChange),
              ld_p    = pvalue,
              ld_q    = padj)
}

tidy_aldex <- function(ad_df) {
  ad_df %>%
    transmute(genus   = taxon,             # already bare in your output
              ad_diff = diff_btw,
              ad_eff  = effect,
              ad_sign = sign(effect),
              ad_p    = we.ep,
              ad_q    = we.eBH)
}

# ---- combine + tier --------------------------------------------------------

build_consensus <- function(maaslin_path, linda_obj, aldex_df, cohort_label) {
  ml <- tidy_maaslin3(maaslin_path)
  ld <- tidy_linda(linda_obj)
  ad <- tidy_aldex(aldex_df)
  
  ml %>%
    full_join(ld, by = "genus") %>%
    full_join(ad, by = "genus") %>%
    filter(!grepl(placeholder_pat, genus)) %>%
    mutate(
      n_q10 = (!is.na(ml_q) & ml_q < 0.10) +
              (!is.na(ld_q) & ld_q < 0.10) +
              (!is.na(ad_q) & ad_q < 0.10),
      n_p05 = (!is.na(ml_p) & ml_p < 0.05) +
              (!is.na(ld_p) & ld_p < 0.05) +
              (!is.na(ad_p) & ad_p < 0.05),
      n_pos = replace_na(ml_sign > 0, FALSE) +
              replace_na(ld_sign > 0, FALSE) +
              replace_na(ad_sign > 0, FALSE),
      n_neg = replace_na(ml_sign < 0, FALSE) +
              replace_na(ld_sign < 0, FALSE) +
              replace_na(ad_sign < 0, FALSE),
      sign_concord = (n_pos > 0 & n_neg == 0) | (n_neg > 0 & n_pos == 0),
      direction = case_when(
        n_pos > 0 & n_neg == 0 ~ "R-enriched",
        n_neg > 0 & n_pos == 0 ~ "NR-enriched",
        n_pos > 0 & n_neg  > 0 ~ "mixed",
        TRUE ~ "untested"
      ),
      tier = case_when(
        n_q10 >= 2 & sign_concord ~ "Strong",
        n_q10 >= 1 & n_p05 >= 2 & sign_concord ~ "Moderate",
        n_p05 >= 2 & sign_concord ~ "Suggestive",
        n_p05 >= 1 ~ "Nominal",
        TRUE ~ "None"
      ),
      cohort = cohort_label
    ) %>%
    arrange(factor(tier, levels = c("Strong","Moderate","Suggestive","Nominal","None")),
            pmin(replace_na(ml_q,1), replace_na(ld_q,1), replace_na(ad_q,1)))
}

con_sheba <- build_consensus(
  file.path(paths$out_dir, "maaslin3_sheba_genus_v4/all_results.tsv"),
  linda_sheba, aldex_sheba, "Sheba")

con_pitt <- build_consensus(
  file.path(paths$out_dir, "maaslin3_pitt_genus/all_results.tsv"),
  linda_pitt,  aldex_pitt,  "Pitt")

# ---- cross-cohort concordance ---------------------------------------------

both <- full_join(
  con_sheba %>% select(genus, dir_S = direction, tier_S = tier,
                       n_p05_S = n_p05, n_q10_S = n_q10),
  con_pitt  %>% select(genus, dir_P = direction, tier_P = tier,
                       n_p05_P = n_p05, n_q10_P = n_q10),
  by = "genus"
) %>%
  mutate(
    cross = case_when(
      dir_S == "R-enriched"  & dir_P == "R-enriched"  & (n_p05_S >= 1 | n_p05_P >= 1) ~ "concordant_R",
      dir_S == "NR-enriched" & dir_P == "NR-enriched" & (n_p05_S >= 1 | n_p05_P >= 1) ~ "concordant_NR",
      (dir_S == "R-enriched"  & dir_P == "NR-enriched") |
      (dir_S == "NR-enriched" & dir_P == "R-enriched") ~ "discordant",
      TRUE ~ "weak/single-cohort"
    )
  )

# ---- summary tables --------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n=== Sheba consensus by tier ===\n")
print(con_sheba %>% count(tier, direction))
cat("\n=== Pitt consensus by tier ===\n")
print(con_pitt  %>% count(tier, direction))
cat("\n=== Cross-cohort concordance (p<0.05 in at least one cohort) ===\n")
print(both %>% filter(cross %in% c("concordant_R","concordant_NR","discordant")) %>%
      count(cross))

cat("\n--- Sheba: Moderate or better ---\n")
print(con_sheba %>% filter(tier %in% c("Strong","Moderate")) %>%
      select(genus, direction, ml_p, ml_q, ld_p, ld_q, ad_p, ad_q))
cat("\n--- Pitt: Moderate or better ---\n")
print(con_pitt %>% filter(tier %in% c("Strong","Moderate")) %>%
      select(genus, direction, ml_p, ml_q, ld_p, ld_q, ad_p, ad_q))

# Save for downstream heatmap
write_tsv(con_sheba, file.path(paths$out_dir, "consensus_sheba.tsv"))
write_tsv(con_pitt,  file.path(paths$out_dir, "consensus_pitt.tsv"))
write_tsv(both,      file.path(paths$out_dir, "consensus_cross_cohort.tsv"))

# 1. The 8 cross-cohort concordant — the replicating signals
cat("\n=== 8 cross-cohort concordant genera ===\n")
both %>%
  filter(cross %in% c("concordant_R","concordant_NR")) %>%
  left_join(con_sheba %>% select(genus, ml_p_S=ml_p, ld_p_S=ld_p, ad_p_S=ad_p,
                                 ml_q_S=ml_q, ld_q_S=ld_q, ad_q_S=ad_q),
            by="genus") %>%
  left_join(con_pitt  %>% select(genus, ml_p_P=ml_p, ld_p_P=ld_p, ad_p_P=ad_p,
                                 ml_q_P=ml_q, ld_q_P=ld_q, ad_q_P=ad_q),
            by="genus") %>%
  arrange(cross, pmin(replace_na(ml_p_S,1), replace_na(ld_p_S,1), replace_na(ad_p_S,1),
                      replace_na(ml_p_P,1), replace_na(ld_p_P,1), replace_na(ad_p_P,1))) %>%
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)

# 2. Suggestive+ in either cohort — the heatmap candidate set
cat("\n=== Suggestive+ in Sheba (Moderate + Suggestive) ===\n")
print(con_sheba %>% filter(tier %in% c("Strong","Moderate","Suggestive")) %>%
      select(genus, tier, direction, ml_p, ld_p, ad_p), n = Inf)
cat("\n=== Suggestive+ in Pitt ===\n")
print(con_pitt  %>% filter(tier %in% c("Strong","Moderate","Suggestive")) %>%
      select(genus, tier, direction, ml_p, ld_p, ad_p), n = Inf)

# 3. Sanity-check the 59 discordant — are they driven by within-cohort method 
#    sign concordance, or are some "discordant" only because one method in one
#    cohort happens to flip? Useful to know before discussing them in methods.
cat("\n=== Discordant breakdown ===\n")
both %>%
  filter(cross == "discordant") %>%
  count(n_p05_S, n_p05_P) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r}
# ---- §8: Heatmap of consensus-supported genera -----------------------------
# ============================================================================
# §8: Consensus heatmaps
# ============================================================================
# Two heatmaps from the 3-method consensus (MaAsLin3 + LinDA + ALDEx2):
#   §8a — 10-feature heatmap of Suggestive+ consensus genera (headline)
#   §8b — wider Nominal+ heatmap organized by evidence block (predicate
#         for the "cohorts are distinct" framing)
#
# Inputs (from §7c-d):
#   sheba_qc, pitt_qc      microeco objects (post-QC)
#   con_sheba, con_pitt    per-cohort consensus tables
#   both                   cross-cohort concordance table
# ============================================================================

library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
library(tidyverse)

# ---- Shared helpers --------------------------------------------------------

placeholder_pat <- "^g__(GGB|FGB|OFGB|CFGB)"

# Per-sample CLR using full QC-filtered genus set as the reference
get_genus_abund <- function(m) {
  ga <- as.data.frame(m$taxa_abund$Genus)
  ga$genus_bare <- sub(".*\\|", "", rownames(ga))
  ga %>%
    group_by(genus_bare) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
    column_to_rownames("genus_bare")
}

clr_full <- function(ab) {
  pc <- min(ab[ab > 0]) / 2
  log_ab <- log(ab + pc)
  apply(log_ab, 2, function(z) z - mean(z))
}

align_features <- function(clr_mat, feats) {
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(feats), ncol = ncol(clr_mat),
                dimnames = list(feats, colnames(clr_mat)))
  ix <- intersect(feats, rownames(clr_mat))
  out[ix, ] <- clr_mat[ix, ]
  out
}

# Sample annotation (Cohort × Response grouping)
build_col_anno <- function(m, cohort_label) {
  st <- as.data.frame(m$sample_table)
  st$SampleID <- rownames(st)
  data.frame(
    SampleID = st$SampleID,
    Cohort   = cohort_label,
    Response = st$Response,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# ---- Build the per-cohort CLR matrices once --------------------------------

ab_S  <- get_genus_abund(sheba_qc)
ab_P  <- get_genus_abund(pitt_qc)
clr_S <- clr_full(ab_S)
clr_P <- clr_full(ab_P)

col_anno <- bind_rows(
  build_col_anno(sheba_qc, "Sheba"),
  build_col_anno(pitt_qc,  "Pitt")
) %>%
  mutate(grp = factor(paste(Cohort, Response, sep = "_"),
                      levels = c("Sheba_Non_responder", "Sheba_Responder",
                                 "Pitt_Non_responder",  "Pitt_Responder"))) %>%
  arrange(grp)

# Shared color palette
response_col <- c(Non_responder = "#e31a1c", Responder = "#1f78b4")
clr_palette  <- colorRamp2(c(-2, 0, 2), c("#2166ac", "#f7f7f7", "#b2182b"))

ha_top_min <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Response = col_anno$Response,
  col = list(Response = response_col),
  annotation_name_side = "left"
)

# ============================================================================
# §8a: 10-feature consensus heatmap (headline)
# ============================================================================

features_10 <- c(
  "g__Slackia", "g__Flavonifractor", "g__Eggerthella", "g__Hungatella",
  "g__Clostridiaceae_unclassified", "g__Lachnospira",

  "g__Actinomyces", "g__Candidatus_Borkfalkia"
)

direction_lookup <- c(
  "g__Slackia"                     = "NR-enriched",
  "g__Flavonifractor"              = "R-enriched",
  "g__Eggerthella"                 = "R-enriched",
  "g__Hungatella"                  = "R-enriched",
  "g__Clostridiaceae_unclassified" = "R-enriched",
  "g__Lachnospira"                 = "R-enriched",
  "g__Flintibacter"                = "R-enriched",
  "g__Oscillibacter"               = "R-enriched",
  "g__Actinomyces"                 = "NR-enriched",
  "g__Candidatus_Borkfalkia"       = "R-enriched"
)

mat_10 <- cbind(align_features(clr_S, features_10),
                align_features(clr_P, features_10))[, col_anno$SampleID]
mat_10z <- t(scale(t(mat_10)))

display_10 <- sub("^g__", "", rownames(mat_10z))
display_10 <- sub("Candidatus_Borkfalkia", "Ca. Borkfalkia", display_10)
rownames(mat_10z) <- display_10

ht_10 <- Heatmap(
  mat_10z,
  name = "CLR z-score",
  col  = clr_palette,
  na_col = "#dddddd",
  top_annotation = ha_top_min,
  column_split   = col_anno$grp,

                          levels = c("NR-enriched", "R-enriched")),
  cluster_columns       = FALSE,
  cluster_column_slices = FALSE,
  cluster_rows          = TRUE,
  cluster_row_slices    = FALSE,
  show_column_names = FALSE,
  row_names_side    = "right",
  row_title         = NULL,
  column_title_gp   = gpar(fontsize = 10, fontface = "bold"),
  heatmap_legend_param = list(direction = "horizontal")
)

svg(file.path(paths$out_dir, "heatmap_consensus_genera.svg"),
    width = 12, height = 4.5)
draw(ht_10, merge_legend = TRUE, heatmap_legend_side = "bottom")
dev.off()
png(file.path(paths$out_dir, "heatmap_consensus_genera.png"),
    width = 12, height = 4.5, units = "in", res = 300)
draw(ht_10, merge_legend = TRUE, heatmap_legend_side = "bottom")
dev.off()

# ============================================================================
# §8b: Wider Nominal+ heatmap, organized by evidence block
# ============================================================================

nom_levels <- c("Strong", "Moderate", "Suggestive", "Nominal")

s_nom <- con_sheba %>%
  filter(tier %in% nom_levels) %>%
  select(genus, tier_S = tier, dir_S = direction)

p_nom <- con_pitt %>%
  filter(tier %in% nom_levels) %>%
  select(genus, tier_P = tier, dir_P = direction)

# ---- Build feat_tbl: combine bilateral + per-cohort genus hits ----
# Modeled on the pathway-level construction at §9A (L2265): bilateral set is
# the inner join with concordant direction; "Sheba-only" / "Pitt-only" are
# the anti-joins. Single `block` column drives row splits and strength scoring.
bilateral_nom_genus <- inner_join(s_nom, p_nom, by = "genus") %>%
  filter(dir_S == dir_P, dir_S != "mixed") %>%
  transmute(genus, source = "Bilateral_nom")

s_only_genus <- s_nom %>%
  filter(!genus %in% p_nom$genus) %>%
  transmute(genus, source = "Sheba_only")

p_only_genus <- p_nom %>%
  filter(!genus %in% s_nom$genus) %>%
  transmute(genus, source = "Pitt_only")

feat_tbl <- bind_rows(
  bilateral_nom_genus,
  s_only_genus,
  p_only_genus
) %>%
  distinct(genus, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(block = case_when(
    source == "Bilateral_nom" ~ "Bilateral",
    source == "Sheba_only"    ~ "Sheba-only",
    source == "Pitt_only"     ~ "Pitt-only"
  ))

cat("\nGenus evidence blocks:\n")
print(table(feat_tbl$block, useNA = "ifany"))

# ---- Order rows within each block by R-vs-NR strength ----
   row_strength <- function(genus, cohort_clr, sample_table) {
     if (!genus %in% rownames(cohort_clr)) return(NA_real_)
     v <- cohort_clr[genus, ]
     resp <- sample_table$Response[match(names(v), rownames(sample_table))]
     mean(v[resp == "Responder"], na.rm = TRUE) -
       mean(v[resp == "Non_responder"], na.rm = TRUE)
   }
   feat_tbl <- feat_tbl %>%
     rowwise() %>%
     mutate(strength = case_when(
       block == "Sheba-only" ~ row_strength(genus, clr_S, as.data.frame(sheba_qc$sample_table)),
       block == "Pitt-only"  ~ row_strength(genus, clr_P, as.data.frame(pitt_qc$sample_table)),
       block == "Bilateral"  ~ (row_strength(genus, clr_S, as.data.frame(sheba_qc$sample_table)) +
                                row_strength(genus, clr_P, as.data.frame(pitt_qc$sample_table))) / 2
     )) %>%
     ungroup() %>%
     arrange(factor(block, levels = c("Sheba-only", "Bilateral", "Pitt-only")),
             desc(strength))   # R-enriched on top, NR-enriched on bottom

cat("\nFeatures by block:\n")
print(table(feat_tbl$block))
cat("Total features:", nrow(feat_tbl), "\n")

features_wide <- feat_tbl$genus

feat_tbl <- feat_tbl %>% filter(genus != "g__Klebsiella")
features_wide <- feat_tbl$genus

mat_w <- cbind(align_features(clr_S, features_wide),
               align_features(clr_P, features_wide))[, col_anno$SampleID]
mat_wz <- t(scale(t(mat_w)))

display_w <- sub("^g__", "", features_wide)
display_w <- sub("Candidatus_Borkfalkia", "Ca. Borkfalkia", display_w)
display_w <- sub("_unclassified", " (unclassified)", display_w)
rownames(mat_wz) <- display_w

ht_wide <- Heatmap(
  mat_wz,
  name = "CLR z-score",
  col  = clr_palette,
  na_col = "#dddddd",
  top_annotation = ha_top_min,
  column_split   = col_anno$grp,
  row_split      = factor(feat_tbl$block,
                          levels = c("Sheba-only", "Bilateral", "Pitt-only")),
  cluster_columns       = FALSE,
  cluster_column_slices = FALSE,
  cluster_rows          = FALSE,
  cluster_row_slices    = FALSE,
  show_column_names = FALSE,
  row_names_side    = "right",
  row_title_gp      = gpar(fontsize = 11, fontface = "bold"),
  column_title_gp   = gpar(fontsize = 10, fontface = "bold"),
  heatmap_legend_param = list(direction = "horizontal")
)

svg(file.path(paths$out_dir, "heatmap_cohort_distinct.svg"),
    width = 13, height = 8)

    width = 13, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300)

    "  heatmap_cohort_distinct.[svg|png]\n", sep = "")
```

# 9. HUMAnN pathway analysis per cohort

We use the unstratified `pathabundance_relab` file directly. **Don't**
re-derive pathway abundances by summing EC numbers — HUMAnN's pathway
calculation accounts for pathway hierarchy and gap-filling.

# ============================================================================
# §9.0  Load + clean + harmonize HUMAnN pathabundance (both cohorts)
# ============================================================================
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

paths$humann_dir <- file.path(dirname(paths$out_dir),
                              "metagenomics_pipeline_input")

# ---- Sheba sample-ID mapper ---------------------------------------------

clean_sheba_humann_id <- function(x) {
  x <- sub("\r$", "", x)
  x <- sub("_R1_kneaddata_merged_Abundance$", "", x)
  x <- sub("_filtered$", "", x)
  if (grepl("^96_ME$",  x)) return("p96A")
  if (grepl("^96_S2$",  x)) return("p96B")
  if (grepl("^177_ME$", x)) return("p177B")
  patient <- sub("^([0-9]+[a-zA-Z]?).*", "\\1", x)
  paste0("p", toupper(patient))
}

clean_pitt_humann_id <- function(x) {
  x <- sub("^trimmed_", "", x)
  x <- sub("_merged_Abundance$", "", x)
  x
}

# ---- Loader ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Reads the merged HUMAnN file, applies the per-cohort sample-ID cleaner,
# averages p96A+p96B for Sheba, returns a numeric data frame keyed by
# 'pathway' column.

load_humann <- function(path, cohort) {
  df <- read_tsv(path, comment = "", col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>%
    rename(pathway = 1) %>%
    filter(pathway != "# Pathway HUMAnN v4.0.0.alpha.1") %>%
    mutate(across(-pathway, as.numeric))
  
  cleaner <- switch(cohort,
                    "Pitt"  = clean_pitt_humann_id,
                    "Sheba" = clean_sheba_humann_id,
                    stop("unknown cohort"))
  
  new_names <- vapply(colnames(df)[-1], cleaner, character(1))
  colnames(df)[-1] <- new_names
  
  if (cohort == "Sheba" && all(c("p96A", "p96B") %in% colnames(df))) {
    df$p96_avg <- (df$p96A + df$p96B) / 2
    df <- df %>% select(-p96A, -p96B)
    cat("[Sheba] averaged p96A + p96B -> p96_avg\n")
  }
  
  cat("[", cohort, "] loaded:", ncol(df) - 1, "samples,",
      nrow(df), "rows total\n")
  df
}

humann_pitt  <- load_humann(file.path(paths$humann_dir,
                                      "merged_pittsburgh_pathabunance.tsv"),
                            "Pitt")
humann_sheba <- load_humann(file.path(paths$humann_dir,
                                      "pathabundance_merged_relab.tsv"),
                            "Sheba")

# ---- Splitter + prep -----------------------------------------------------
# Splits a HUMAnN frame into (unstratified, stratified) matrices, subsets to
# the QC sample set, drops UNMAPPED/UNINTEGRATED from unstratified,
# renormalizes unstratified per-sample to relab among classified pathways.
# Stratified is kept on its raw scale (we'll renormalize at follow-up time).

prep_humann <- function(df, expected_samples, cohort_label) {
  
  # Subset columns to QC samples
  keep    <- intersect(colnames(df)[-1], expected_samples)
  dropped <- setdiff(colnames(df)[-1], expected_samples)
  cat("\n[", cohort_label, "] keeping", length(keep), "samples; dropping",
      length(dropped),
      if (length(dropped)) paste0("(", paste(dropped, collapse = ", "), ")") else "",
      "\n")
  df <- df %>% select(pathway, all_of(keep))
  
  # Split unstratified vs stratified
  is_strat <- grepl("\\|", df$pathway)
  unstrat_df <- df %>% filter(!is_strat,
                              !pathway %in% c("UNMAPPED", "UNINTEGRATED"))
  strat_df   <- df %>% filter(is_strat)
  
  # Build unstratified matrix
  m_u <- as.matrix(unstrat_df[, -1, drop = FALSE])
  rownames(m_u) <- unstrat_df$pathway
  
  # Drop all-zero rows post-subset
  zr <- rowSums(m_u) == 0
  if (any(zr)) {
    cat("  Dropped", sum(zr), "all-zero unstratified pathways post-subset\n")
    m_u <- m_u[!zr, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  
  # Per-sample renormalize (relab among classified pathways)
  cs <- colSums(m_u)
  if (any(cs == 0)) cat("  WARNING: zero-yield samples:",
                        paste(colnames(m_u)[cs == 0], collapse = ", "), "\n")
  m_u <- sweep(m_u, 2, ifelse(cs == 0, 1, cs), "/")
  
  # Stratified matrix (keep separately, no renorm — stratified contributions
  # are fractions of their pathway, never DA features in their own right)
  m_s <- as.matrix(strat_df[, -1, drop = FALSE])
  rownames(m_s) <- strat_df$pathway
  
  cat("  Unstratified:", nrow(m_u), "pathways x", ncol(m_u), "samples\n")
  cat("  Stratified:  ", nrow(m_s), "rows x",      ncol(m_s), "samples\n")
  
  list(unstrat = m_u, strat = m_s)
}

path_pitt  <- prep_humann(humann_pitt,  rownames(pitt_qc$sample_table),  "Pitt")
path_sheba <- prep_humann(humann_sheba, rownames(sheba_qc$sample_table), "Sheba")

# ---- Sanity checks --------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n--- Column sum range (unstratified, should be ~1) ---\n")
cat("Pitt:  ", paste(round(range(colSums(path_pitt$unstrat)),  4)), "\n")
cat("Sheba: ", paste(round(range(colSums(path_sheba$unstrat)), 4)), "\n")

cat("\n--- Pathway count comparison ---\n")
cat("Pitt unstrat:  ", nrow(path_pitt$unstrat), "\n")
cat("Sheba unstrat: ", nrow(path_sheba$unstrat), "\n")
cat("Shared:        ",
    length(intersect(rownames(path_pitt$unstrat),
                     rownames(path_sheba$unstrat))), "\n")
cat("Pitt-only:     ",
    length(setdiff(rownames(path_pitt$unstrat),
                   rownames(path_sheba$unstrat))), "\n")
cat("Sheba-only:    ",
    length(setdiff(rownames(path_sheba$unstrat),
                   rownames(path_pitt$unstrat))), "\n")

# ---- Save -----------------------------------------------------------------
saveRDS(list(pitt = path_pitt, sheba = path_sheba),
        file.path(paths$out_dir, "humann_pathway_data.rds"))


```

# ============================================================================
# §9.1  Filter unstratified pathways (prev ≥10%, abundance ≥1e-4)
# ============================================================================
```{r}
filter_pathway_mat <- function(mat, prev_thresh = 0.10, abund_thresh = 1e-4,
                               label = "") {
  prev <- rowMeans(mat > 0)
  ma   <- rowMeans(mat)
  keep <- prev >= prev_thresh & ma >= abund_thresh
  
  cat(label, ": pre-filter ", nrow(mat),
      "; below prev ", prev_thresh, ": ", sum(prev < prev_thresh),
      "; below mean ", abund_thresh, ": ", sum(ma < abund_thresh),
      "; post-filter ", sum(keep), "\n", sep = "")
  
  mat[keep, , drop = FALSE]
}

path_pitt_f  <- filter_pathway_mat(path_pitt$unstrat,  label = "Pitt ")
path_sheba_f <- filter_pathway_mat(path_sheba$unstrat, label = "Sheba")

# ============================================================================
# §9.2  Pathway β-diversity (Aitchison primary; same framework as §6)
# ============================================================================

library(vegan); library(ape); library(ggplot2); library(patchwork)

run_pathway_beta <- function(mat_f, sample_table, formula_rhs, label,
                             permdisp_groups = "Response") {
  ab <- t(mat_f)                                  # samples × features
  pc <- min(ab[ab > 0]) / 2                       # half-min-nonzero pseudocount
  cl <- log(ab + pc)
  cl <- t(apply(cl, 1, function(x) x - mean(x))) # CLR
  d  <- dist(cl, method = "euclidean")            # Aitchison
  
  md <- as.data.frame(sample_table[rownames(ab), , drop = FALSE])
  
  # PERMANOVA marginal
  set.seed(42)
  ad <- adonis2(as.formula(paste("d ~", formula_rhs)),
                data = md, permutations = PARAMS$permanova_perms, by = "margin")
  
  # PERMDISP for each requested group
  pd <- lapply(permdisp_groups, function(g) {
    if (!g %in% colnames(md)) return(NULL)
    permutest(betadisper(d, md[[g]]),
              permutations = PARAMS$permanova_perms)
  })
  names(pd) <- permdisp_groups
  
  # PCoA
  ord <- pcoa(d)
  eig <- 100 * ord$values$Relative_eig
  df  <- data.frame(Axis1 = ord$vectors[, 1],
                    Axis2 = ord$vectors[, 2],
                    Response = md$Response)
  
  resp_p  <- ad["Response", "Pr(>F)"]
  resp_r2 <- ad["Response", "R2"]
  pd_resp <- pd$Response$tab[1, "Pr(>F)"]
  
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(Axis1, Axis2, color = Response)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
    stat_ellipse(type = "t", level = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Non_responder = "#e31a1c",
                                  Responder     = "#1f78b4")) +
    labs(title = paste0(label, ": Pathway Aitchison PCoA"),
         subtitle = sprintf("Response R²=%.3f, p=%.3f | PERMDISP-Response p=%.3f",
                            resp_r2, resp_p, pd_resp),
         x = sprintf("PCoA1 (%.1f%%)", eig[1]),
         y = sprintf("PCoA2 (%.1f%%)", eig[2])) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12)
  
  list(adonis = ad, permdisp = pd, plot = p, distance = d, eig = eig)
}

beta_path_pitt  <- run_pathway_beta(
  path_pitt_f, pitt_qc$sample_table,
  "Response + Sequencing_Batch + Treatment_regimen",
  "Pitt", permdisp_groups = c("Response", "Sequencing_Batch"))

beta_path_sheba <- run_pathway_beta(
  path_sheba_f, sheba_qc$sample_table,
  "Response + Treatment_regimen",
  "Sheba", permdisp_groups = "Response")

# ---- Print PERMANOVA tables --------------------------------------------
cat("\n========== PITT PATHWAY PERMANOVA (marginal) ==========\n")
print(beta_path_pitt$adonis)
cat("\nPERMDISP Response : p =",
    beta_path_pitt$permdisp$Response$tab[1, "Pr(>F)"], "\n")
cat("PERMDISP Batch    : p =",
    beta_path_pitt$permdisp$Sequencing_Batch$tab[1, "Pr(>F)"], "\n")

cat("\n========== SHEBA PATHWAY PERMANOVA (marginal) ==========\n")
print(beta_path_sheba$adonis)
cat("\nPERMDISP Response : p =",
    beta_path_sheba$permdisp$Response$tab[1, "Pr(>F)"], "\n")

# ---- Side-by-side comparison with genus β-diversity --------------------
cat("\n========== GENUS vs PATHWAY (Aitchison, Response marginal) ==========\n")
cat(sprintf("Sheba  | genus   R²=3.6%%  p=0.088\n"))
cat(sprintf("Sheba  | pathway R²=%.1f%%  p=%.3f\n",
            100 * beta_path_sheba$adonis["Response", "R2"],
            beta_path_sheba$adonis["Response", "Pr(>F)"]))
cat(sprintf("Pitt   | genus   R²=1.5%%  p=0.33\n"))
cat(sprintf("Pitt   | pathway R²=%.1f%%  p=%.3f\n",
            100 * beta_path_pitt$adonis["Response", "R2"],
            beta_path_pitt$adonis["Response", "Pr(>F)"]))

# ---- Save plots --------------------------------------------------------
ggsave(file.path(paths$out_dir, "pcoa_pathway_pitt.svg"),
       beta_path_pitt$plot, width = 7, height = 5.5)
ggsave(file.path(paths$out_dir, "pcoa_pathway_sheba.svg"),
       beta_path_sheba$plot, width = 7, height = 5.5)

beta_path_pitt$plot | beta_path_sheba$plot
```

```{r}
dir.create(file.path(paths$out_dir, "humann_da"), showWarnings = FALSE)

# ---- MaAsLin3 ----------------------------------------------------------
# Pathways arrive as relab; MaAsLin3's TSS normalization is a no-op on these,
# but we keep it to match §7 conventions. transform = "LOG" for log-relab.

run_maaslin3_path <- function(mat_f, sample_table, output_dir, formula,
                              reference = "Non_responder") {
  abund <- as.data.frame(t(mat_f))
  metad <- as.data.frame(sample_table)
  
  # Subset metadata to fixed-effect columns (the bug fix from §7)
  fe <- all.vars(as.formula(paste("~", formula)))
  metad <- metad[, fe, drop = FALSE]
  metad$Response <- relevel(factor(metad$Response), ref = reference)
  
  # Align rows
  shared <- intersect(rownames(abund), rownames(metad))
  abund  <- abund[shared, , drop = FALSE]
  metad  <- metad[shared, , drop = FALSE]
  
  maaslin3::maaslin3(
    input_data       = abund,
    input_metadata   = metad,
    output           = output_dir,
    formula          = paste("~", formula),
    normalization    = "TSS",
    transform        = "LOG",
    correction       = "BH",
    min_abundance    = 0,        # already filtered upstream
    min_prevalence   = 0,
    max_significance = 0.10,
    cores            = 2,
    plot_summary_plot   = TRUE,
    plot_associations   = TRUE
  )
}

# THESE TWO ARE CALLED FOR THEIR SIDE EFFECT, not for what they return. The
# return value is never used -- the results are read back from disk on the
# lines below -- but the call is what WRITES
# humann_da/maaslin3_{sheba,pitt}_pathway/all_results.tsv, and those two files
# are the pathway scan that Extended Data Fig. 2 draws and whose feature counts
# the Results quote. A linter will call the assignments unused. Do not remove
# them, and do not reduce them to bare calls without keeping the paths.
ml_path_sheba <- run_maaslin3_path(
  path_sheba_f, sheba_qc$sample_table,
  file.path(paths$out_dir, "humann_da/maaslin3_sheba_pathway"),
  "Response + Treatment_regimen")

ml_path_pitt <- run_maaslin3_path(
  path_pitt_f, pitt_qc$sample_table,
  file.path(paths$out_dir, "humann_da/maaslin3_pitt_pathway"),
  "Response + Sequencing_Batch + Treatment_regimen")

ml_sheba_res <- read_tsv(
  file.path(paths$out_dir, "humann_da/maaslin3_sheba_pathway/all_results.tsv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)
ml_pitt_res <- read_tsv(
  file.path(paths$out_dir, "humann_da/maaslin3_pitt_pathway/all_results.tsv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)

cat("\n========== Sheba MaAsLin3 top 15 (Response, abundance) ==========\n")
print(ml_sheba_res %>% 
      filter(metadata == "Response", model == "abundance") %>%
      arrange(pval_individual) %>%

cat("\n========== Pitt MaAsLin3 top 15 (Response, abundance) ==========\n")
print(ml_pitt_res %>%

print(ml_sheba_res %>% 
      filter(metadata == "Response", model == "prevalence") %>%

      select(feature, coef, pval_individual, qval_individual) %>%

cat("\n========== Pitt MaAsLin3 top 15 (Response, prevalence) ==========\n")
print(ml_pitt_res %>% 
      filter(metadata == "Response", model == "prevalence") %>%
      arrange(pval_individual) %>% 
      select(feature, coef, pval_individual, qval_individual) %>%
      head(15), n = 15)

# ---- LinDA -------------------------------------------------------------

run_linda_path <- function(mat_f, sample_table, formula_rhs) {
  feat <- as.data.frame(mat_f)
  meta <- as.data.frame(sample_table)
  shared <- intersect(colnames(feat), rownames(meta))
  feat <- feat[, shared, drop = FALSE]
  meta <- meta[shared, , drop = FALSE]
  
  MicrobiomeStat::linda(
    feature.dat       = feat,
    meta.dat          = meta,
    formula           = paste("~", formula_rhs),
    feature.dat.type  = "proportion",
    prev.filter       = 0,           # already filtered
    mean.abund.filter = 0,
    adaptive          = TRUE,
    p.adj.method      = "BH",
    alpha             = 0.10
  )
}

ld_path_sheba <- run_linda_path(path_sheba_f, sheba_qc$sample_table,
                                "Response + Treatment_regimen")
ld_path_pitt  <- run_linda_path(path_pitt_f,  pitt_qc$sample_table,
                                "Response + Sequencing_Batch + Treatment_regimen")

ld_s <- as.data.frame(ld_path_sheba$output[[
  grep("Response", names(ld_path_sheba$output), value = TRUE)[1]]]) %>%
  rownames_to_column("pathway") %>% arrange(pvalue)
ld_p <- as.data.frame(ld_path_pitt$output[[
  grep("Response", names(ld_path_pitt$output),  value = TRUE)[1]]]) %>%
  rownames_to_column("pathway") %>% arrange(pvalue)

cat("\n========== LinDA Sheba top 15 ==========\n")
print(as.data.frame(ld_s %>% select(pathway, log2FoldChange, pvalue, padj) %>% head(15)))
cat("\n========== LinDA Pitt top 15 ==========\n")
print(as.data.frame(ld_p %>% select(pathway, log2FoldChange, pvalue, padj) %>% head(15)))


# ---- ALDEx2 ------------------------------------------------------------
# ALDEx2 wants integer-like counts. Pathway relab values are 0–1; we scale by
# a constant (1e6 → CPM-like) and round. Per-sample column sums become equal
# (1e6) which doesn't bother ALDEx2's CLR transform.

run_aldex2_path <- function(mat_f, sample_table, scale_to = 1e6) {
  shared <- intersect(colnames(mat_f), rownames(sample_table))
  mat_f  <- mat_f[, shared, drop = FALSE]
  cond   <- as.character(sample_table[shared, "Response"])
  
  counts <- round(mat_f * scale_to)
  counts <- counts[rowSums(counts) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  
  set.seed(42)
  # Step 1: CLR Monte Carlo instances
  clr <- ALDEx2::aldex.clr(counts, conds = cond, mc.samples = 128, denom = "all")
  # Step 2: t-test (gives we.ep, we.eBH, wi.ep, wi.eBH)
  tt  <- ALDEx2::aldex.ttest(clr, paired.test = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
  # Step 3: effect sizes (gives diff.btw, diff.win, effect, overlap)
  ef  <- ALDEx2::aldex.effect(clr, verbose = FALSE)
  # Merge
  ax  <- cbind(ef, tt)
  ax$pathway  <- rownames(ax)
  ax$passes_q <- ax$we.eBH < 0.10
  
  ax %>%
    select(pathway, diff_btw = diff.btw, diff_win = diff.win,
           effect, overlap, we.ep, we.eBH, wi.ep, wi.eBH, passes_q) %>%
    arrange(we.ep)
}

ax_path_sheba <- run_aldex2_path(path_sheba_f, sheba_qc$sample_table)
ax_path_pitt  <- run_aldex2_path(path_pitt_f,  pitt_qc$sample_table)

# ---- Quick-look summaries ----------------------------------------------
cat("\n========== MaAsLin3 q<0.10 hits ==========\n")
cat("Sheba abundance:",
    sum(ml_sheba_res$model == "abundance" & ml_sheba_res$metadata == "Response"
        & ml_sheba_res$qval_individual < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Pitt  abundance:",
    sum(ml_pitt_res$model == "abundance"  & ml_pitt_res$metadata == "Response"
        & ml_pitt_res$qval_individual < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

cat("\n========== LinDA q<0.10 hits ==========\n")

cat("Sheba:", sum(ld_s$padj < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Pitt :", sum(ld_p$padj < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

cat("\n========== ALDEx2 q<0.10 hits (welch) ==========\n")
cat("Sheba:", sum(ax_path_sheba$passes_q, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Pitt :", sum(ax_path_pitt$passes_q,  na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

cat("\n========== Top 10 by p across methods (Sheba) ==========\n")
print(head(ax_path_sheba , 10))
cat("\n========== Top 10 by p across methods (Pitt) ==========\n")
print(head(ax_path_pitt , 10))
```

```{r}

library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
library(tidyverse)

# ---- Shared infrastructure -----------------------------------------------

clr_pathway <- function(mat) {
  pc <- min(mat[mat > 0]) / 2
  log_mat <- log(mat + pc)
  apply(log_mat, 2, function(z) z - mean(z))
}

clr_pitt_path  <- clr_pathway(path_pitt_f)
clr_sheba_path <- clr_pathway(path_sheba_f)

# Column annotation in shared sample order (Cohort × Response)
col_anno_path <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(SampleID = colnames(path_sheba_f), Cohort = "Sheba",
             Response = as.character(sheba_qc$sample_table[colnames(path_sheba_f), "Response"]),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  data.frame(SampleID = colnames(path_pitt_f),  Cohort = "Pitt",
             Response = as.character(pitt_qc$sample_table[colnames(path_pitt_f), "Response"]),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
) %>%
  mutate(grp = factor(paste(Cohort, Response, sep = "_"),
                      levels = c("Sheba_Non_responder", "Sheba_Responder",
                                 "Pitt_Non_responder",  "Pitt_Responder"))) %>%
  arrange(grp)

response_col  <- c(Non_responder = "#e31a1c", Responder = "#1f78b4")
clr_palette   <- colorRamp2(c(-2, 0, 2), c("#2166ac", "#f7f7f7", "#b2182b"))
ha_top_min    <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Response = col_anno_path$Response,
  col = list(Response = response_col),
  annotation_name_side = "left"
)

align_pathways <- function(clr_mat, feats) {
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(feats), ncol = ncol(clr_mat),
                dimnames = list(feats, colnames(clr_mat)))
  ix <- intersect(feats, rownames(clr_mat))
  out[ix, ] <- clr_mat[ix, ]
  out
}

# Strip "PWY-NNNN: " or "PWYNNNN-PWY: " prefixes from display names
shorten_pwy <- function(x) {
  sub("^[^:]+: *", "", x)
}

# ============================================================================
# §9.5  Pathway figures — 9A: cohort-distinct + bilateral pathway heatmap
# ============================================================================
# Three row blocks:
#   - Sheba-only:  Suggestive+ in Sheba (≥2 methods p<0.05, concordant), not in Pitt
#   - Bilateral:   ≥1 method p<0.10 in BOTH cohorts, concordant direction
#   - Pitt-only:   Suggestive+ in Pitt, not in Sheba
# Bilateral takes precedence over single-cohort blocks for any overlap.
# ============================================================================

library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
library(tidyverse)

# ---- Per-cohort consensus from the 3 methods ------------------------------

ml_pitt_abund  <- ml_pitt_res  %>% filter(metadata == "Response", model == "abundance")
ml_sheba_abund <- ml_sheba_res %>% filter(metadata == "Response", model == "abundance")

pathway_consensus <- function(ml_df, ld_df, ax_df) {
  ml <- ml_df %>% transmute(pathway = feature, ml_p = pval_individual,
                             ml_q = qval_individual, ml_sign = sign(coef))
  ld <- ld_df %>% transmute(pathway, ld_p = pvalue, ld_q = padj,
                             ld_sign = sign(log2FoldChange))
  ax <- ax_df %>% transmute(pathway, ax_p = we.ep, ax_q = we.eBH,
                             ax_sign = sign(effect))
  full_join(ml, ld, by = "pathway") %>%
    full_join(ax, by = "pathway") %>%
    mutate(
      n_p05 = (replace_na(ml_p, 1) < 0.05) +
              (replace_na(ld_p, 1) < 0.05) +
              (replace_na(ax_p, 1) < 0.05),
      n_p10 = (replace_na(ml_p, 1) < 0.10) +
              (replace_na(ld_p, 1) < 0.10) +
              (replace_na(ax_p, 1) < 0.10),
      n_pos = replace_na(ml_sign > 0, FALSE) +
              replace_na(ld_sign > 0, FALSE) +
              replace_na(ax_sign > 0, FALSE),
      n_neg = replace_na(ml_sign < 0, FALSE) +
              replace_na(ld_sign < 0, FALSE) +
              replace_na(ax_sign < 0, FALSE),
      direction = case_when(
        n_pos > 0 & n_neg == 0 ~ "R-enriched",
        n_neg > 0 & n_pos == 0 ~ "NR-enriched",
        TRUE                    ~ "mixed"
      ),
      tier = case_when(
        n_p05 >= 2 & direction != "mixed" ~ "Suggestive",
        n_p05 >= 1                         ~ "Nominal",
        TRUE                                ~ "None"
      )
    )
}

con_path_pitt  <- pathway_consensus(ml_pitt_abund,  ld_p, ax_path_pitt)
con_path_sheba <- pathway_consensus(ml_sheba_abund, ld_s, ax_path_sheba)

# ---- Build the three row blocks -------------------------------------------

# Within-cohort Suggestive+ (strict bar: ≥2 methods p<0.05, concordant)
s_suggestive <- con_path_sheba %>% filter(tier == "Suggestive") %>%
  transmute(pathway, source = "Sheba_sugg")
p_suggestive <- con_path_pitt  %>% filter(tier == "Suggestive") %>%
  transmute(pathway, source = "Pitt_sugg")

# Cross-cohort Bilateral-Nominal (looser bar: ≥1 method p<0.10 in both,
# concordant direction).
bilateral_nom_tbl <- inner_join(
  con_path_sheba %>% filter(n_p10 >= 1) %>% select(pathway, dir_S = direction),
  con_path_pitt  %>% filter(n_p10 >= 1) %>% select(pathway, dir_P = direction),
  by = "pathway"
) %>%
  filter(dir_S == dir_P, dir_S != "mixed") %>%
  transmute(pathway, source = "Bilateral_nom")

cat("\nBilateral-Nominal pathways (≥1 method p<0.10 in both cohorts, concordant):",
    nrow(bilateral_nom_tbl), "\n")
print(bilateral_nom_tbl$pathway)

# Combine; Bilateral takes precedence over single-cohort entries
feat_path_tbl <- bind_rows(
  bilateral_nom_tbl,
  s_suggestive %>% filter(!pathway %in% bilateral_nom_tbl$pathway),
  p_suggestive %>% filter(!pathway %in% bilateral_nom_tbl$pathway)
) %>%
  distinct(pathway, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(block = case_when(
    source == "Bilateral_nom" ~ "Bilateral",
    source == "Sheba_sugg"    ~ "Sheba-only",
    source == "Pitt_sugg"     ~ "Pitt-only"
  ))

cat("\nPathway evidence blocks:\n")
print(table(feat_path_tbl$block, useNA = "ifany"))

# ---- Order rows within each block by R-vs-NR strength ---------------------

row_strength_pwy <- function(pwy, cohort_clr, sample_table) {
  if (!pwy %in% rownames(cohort_clr)) return(NA_real_)
  v <- cohort_clr[pwy, ]
  resp <- sample_table$Response[match(names(v), rownames(sample_table))]
  mean(v[resp == "Responder"], na.rm = TRUE) -
    mean(v[resp == "Non_responder"], na.rm = TRUE)
}

feat_path_tbl <- feat_path_tbl %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(strength = case_when(
    block == "Sheba-only" ~ row_strength_pwy(pathway, clr_sheba_path,
                                              as.data.frame(sheba_qc$sample_table)),
    block == "Pitt-only"  ~ row_strength_pwy(pathway, clr_pitt_path,
                                              as.data.frame(pitt_qc$sample_table)),
    block == "Bilateral"  ~ (row_strength_pwy(pathway, clr_sheba_path,
                                                as.data.frame(sheba_qc$sample_table)) +
                              row_strength_pwy(pathway, clr_pitt_path,
                                                as.data.frame(pitt_qc$sample_table))) / 2
  )) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(factor(block, levels = c("Sheba-only", "Bilateral", "Pitt-only")),
          desc(strength))

features_9A <- feat_path_tbl$pathway

# ---- Build CLR z-score matrix ---------------------------------------------

mat_9A  <- cbind(align_pathways(clr_sheba_path, features_9A),
                 align_pathways(clr_pitt_path,  features_9A))[, col_anno_path$SampleID]
mat_9Az <- t(scale(t(mat_9A)))
rownames(mat_9Az) <- shorten_pwy(rownames(mat_9Az))

# ---- Heatmap --------------------------------------------------------------

ht_9A <- Heatmap(
  mat_9Az,
  name = "CLR z-score",
  col  = clr_palette,
  na_col = "#dddddd",
  top_annotation = ha_top_min,
  column_split   = col_anno_path$grp,
  row_split      = factor(feat_path_tbl$block,
                          levels = c("Sheba-only", "Bilateral", "Pitt-only")),
  cluster_columns       = FALSE, cluster_column_slices = FALSE,
  cluster_rows          = FALSE, cluster_row_slices    = FALSE,
  show_column_names = FALSE,
  row_names_side    = "right",
  row_names_gp      = gpar(fontsize = 8),
  row_title_gp      = gpar(fontsize = 11, fontface = "bold"),
  column_title_gp   = gpar(fontsize = 10, fontface = "bold"),
  heatmap_legend_param = list(direction = "horizontal")
)

fig_height <- max(5, 0.25 * nrow(mat_9Az) + 2)

svg(file.path(paths$out_dir, "heatmap_pathway_cohort_distinct.svg"),
    width = 14, height = fig_height)
draw(ht_9A, merge_legend = TRUE, heatmap_legend_side = "bottom")
dev.off()

png(file.path(paths$out_dir, "heatmap_pathway_cohort_distinct.png"),
    width = 14, height = fig_height, units = "in", res = 300)
draw(ht_9A, merge_legend = TRUE, heatmap_legend_side = "bottom")
dev.off()

cat("\nSaved:\n",
    "  heatmap_pathway_cohort_distinct.[svg|png]\n")
```

```{r}
# 10. Combined microtable
# ============================================================================
# §10  Combined microtable + combined pathway data
# ============================================================================
# Builds two combined data objects on the QC-filtered cohort sets:
#   combo_genus    — microeco microtable, n=103, taxa collapsed to bare genus
#   combo_path     — list with $unstrat (relab matrix) and per-cohort metadata
#
# Both use sheba_qc (n=33) and pitt_qc (n=70) as primary, mirroring the per-
# cohort analyses (locked decision #3).
# ============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(microeco)

# ---- §10a Combined genus microtable --------------------------------------

collapse_to_bare_genus <- function(m) {
  # Returns a list of (otu_table, sample_table, tax_table) with rows keyed by
  # bare genus name (stripped of full lineage). Per locked decision #9 we drop
  # placeholder genera before any analysis.
  ot <- as.data.frame(m$otu_table)
  ot$bare <- sub(".*\\|", "", rownames(ot))
  ot <- ot %>%
    group_by(bare) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
    column_to_rownames("bare")
  
  st <- as.data.frame(m$sample_table)
  
  # Build a minimal tax table at genus level
  tx <- data.frame(Genus = rownames(ot), row.names = rownames(ot),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  list(otu = ot, sample = st, tax = tx)
}

combine_meco_genus <- function(m_a, m_b, label_a = "Sheba", label_b = "Pitt") {

  # ---- sample_table prep ---------------------------------------------
  prep_sm <- function(m, cohort_label) {
    sm <- as.data.frame(m$sample_table)
    if ("SampleID" %in% colnames(sm)) sm$SampleID <- NULL          # avoid collision
    if (!"Cohort" %in% colnames(sm)) sm$Cohort <- cohort_label
    if (!"Treatment_regimen" %in% colnames(sm))
      sm$Treatment_regimen <- NA_character_
    rownames_to_column(sm, "SampleID")
  }

  # ---- bare-genus OTU matrix -----------------------------------------
  # Sheba is species-level lineage, Pitt is genus-level lineage. Strip to
  # last token (g__X) and sum any duplicates so the join keys match.
  prep_otu_genus <- function(m, cohort_label) {
    src <- if (!is.null(m$taxa_abund) && !is.null(m$taxa_abund$Genus))
             m$taxa_abund$Genus else m$otu_table
    ga  <- as.data.frame(src)
    bare <- sub(".*\\|", "", rownames(ga))
    ga  <- as.data.frame(rowsum(as.matrix(ga), group = bare))      # collapse-then-sum
    cat("[", cohort_label, "] genus-collapsed: ", nrow(ga),
        " genera × ", ncol(ga), " samples\n", sep = "")
    rownames_to_column(ga, "Genus")
  }

  ot_a <- prep_otu_genus(m_a, label_a)
  ot_b <- prep_otu_genus(m_b, label_b)

  otu <- full_join(ot_a, ot_b, by = "Genus") %>% column_to_rownames("Genus")
  otu[is.na(otu)] <- 0

  # ---- sample_table merge --------------------------------------------
  sm_a <- prep_sm(m_a, label_a)
  sm_b <- prep_sm(m_b, label_b)

  shared_cols <- intersect(colnames(sm_a), colnames(sm_b))
  cat("\nShared sample_table columns (", length(shared_cols), "):\n  ",
      paste(shared_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n\n", sep = "")
  # ---- type harmonization on shared columns ---------------------------
  # bind_rows fails on type mismatches; coerce to character when classes differ
  for (col in shared_cols) {
    if (!identical(class(sm_a[[col]]), class(sm_b[[col]]))) {
      cat("  ! type mismatch on '", col, "' (",
          class(sm_a[[col]])[1], " vs ", class(sm_b[[col]])[1],
          ") — coercing to character\n", sep = "")
      sm_a[[col]] <- as.character(sm_a[[col]])
      sm_b[[col]] <- as.character(sm_b[[col]])
    }
  }
  required <- c("SampleID", "Response", "Cohort", "Treatment_regimen")
  missing  <- setdiff(required, shared_cols)
  if (length(missing))
    stop("Missing required column(s) after harmonization: ",
         paste(missing, collapse = ", "))

  sm <- bind_rows(sm_a, sm_b) %>% column_to_rownames("SampleID")
  sm <- sm[colnames(otu), , drop = FALSE]

  # ---- tax_table (genus-level minimal, w/ upper ranks where coalescible)
  pull_tx <- function(m) {
    tx <- as.data.frame(m$tax_table)
    if (!"Genus" %in% colnames(tx)) return(NULL)
    tx$Genus_bare <- sub(".*\\|", "", tx$Genus)
    # pick first row per Genus_bare for upper-rank lookup
    tx[!duplicated(tx$Genus_bare), , drop = FALSE]
  }
  tx_a <- pull_tx(m_a); tx_b <- pull_tx(m_b)
  tx <- data.frame(Genus_bare = rownames(otu), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    left_join(tx_a %>% select(Genus_bare, any_of(c("Kingdom","Phylum","Class","Order","Family"))),
              by = "Genus_bare", suffix = c("", ".a")) %>%
    left_join(tx_b %>% select(Genus_bare, any_of(c("Kingdom","Phylum","Class","Order","Family"))),
              by = "Genus_bare", suffix = c(".a", ".b")) %>%
    mutate(Kingdom = coalesce(Kingdom.a, Kingdom.b),
           Phylum  = coalesce(Phylum.a,  Phylum.b),
           Class   = coalesce(Class.a,   Class.b),
           Order   = coalesce(Order.a,   Order.b),
           Family  = coalesce(Family.a,  Family.b),
           Genus   = Genus_bare) %>%
    select(Genus, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family) %>%
    column_to_rownames("Genus")
  tx <- tx[rownames(otu), , drop = FALSE]
  tx$Genus <- rownames(tx)   # microeco wants Genus column present

  m <- microtable$new(otu_table = otu, sample_table = sm, tax_table = tx)
  m$tidy_dataset()
  m
}
```
